# Wireframe glow

Draws glowing lines along every triangle edge at a constant width on screen, over a faint fill or nothing at all. The geometry needs barycentric coordinates: prepare it once with `withBarycentric(geometry)`.

<EffectDemo effect="wireframe" />

## Usage

```ts
import { patchMaterial } from '@mk7s/xtree/core';
import { wireframe } from '@mk7s/xtree/effects/wireframe';

const effect = wireframe({ preset: 'tron' });
patchMaterial(mesh.material, effect);
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => renderer.render(scene, camera));
```

Every parameter is also a property: `effect.lineColor = '#5ad8ff'`. Uniform changes take effect on the next frame without recompiling.

## Parameters

| Parameter     | Type                                                      | Default     | Range       | Description                                                               |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lineColor`   | hex color (theme: [`accent`](/guide/holocss#theme-roles)) | `'#5ad8ff'` |             | Line color.                                                               |
| `glow`        | number                                                    | `2`         | 0 – 10      | Line brightness, in linear units (above 1 blooms).                        |
| `thickness`   | number                                                    | `1.2`       | 0.25 – 6 px | Line width on screen.                                                     |
| `fillColor`   | hex color                                                 | `'#060814'` |             | Color the faces are tinted toward.                                        |
| `fillOpacity` | number                                                    | `0.85`      | 0 – 1       | How far the faces are tinted toward the fill color.                       |
| `hideFill`    | boolean                                                   | `false`     |             | Draw the lines only (pair with additive blending in a scene of your own). |
| `fadeGrazing` | number                                                    | `0.6`       | 0 – 1       | Fade lines on faces seen edge-on.                                         |

Every effect also has `blend` (any of the 26 [blend modes](/reference/shaders#modes)), `opacity` (0–1) and `enabled`.

## Presets

| Preset      | Settings                                                  |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tron`      | `lineColor: '#00e5ff'`, `glow: 3`, `fillOpacity: 0.95`    |
| `blueprint` | `lineColor: '#ffffff'`, `glow: 1`, `fillColor: '#103a7a'` |
| `overlay`   | `fillOpacity: 0`, `glow: 1.2`, `thickness: 1`             |
| `neon`      | `lineColor: '#ff4fd8'`, `glow: 4`, `thickness: 2`         |

Apply one with `wireframe({ preset: 'name' })` or `effect.applyPreset('name')`; presets start from the defaults.

## Details

- **Family:** Materials · tracked as story X12.6 in the [plan](https://github.com/s4njee/xtree/blob/main/plan.md).
- **Kind:** material effect. `patchMaterial(material, effect)` splices it into MeshBasic, Lambert, Phong, Standard, Physical, Toon and Matcap materials, so lighting, fog and shadows keep working; `unpatchMaterial` removes it. See [material effects](/guide/materials).
- **Motion:** Static: nothing animates.
- **Size:** 6.1 KB gzip budget for `@mk7s/xtree/effects/wireframe`, including the shared effect runtime.

## Credits

Original implementation (MIT). References: Barycentric wireframe with screen-space derivatives, after Bærentzen et al., Single-pass wireframe rendering, 2006.
